newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine firm to launch proceeding against Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Argentine firm to launch proceeding against Brazil.

text.p: Argentine construction group Roggio SA said Thursday it will launch a discrimination complaint against Brazil in what is the first dispute settlement test of its kind in the Mercosur customs union.
Roggio spokesman Juan Ordonoz told Reuters the group will use a Mercosur protocol to start proceedings in what it claims to be unfair treatment in Brazilian privatization tenders.
Mercosur is a two-year old customs union between Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay.
Some Argentine firms, notably in the financial services sector, have complained about unfair treatment by Brazilian authorities in their efforts to break into Brazil's markets.

"We are experiencing in Brazil a systematic process of disqualification in the tenders for concessions for toll roads where we are taking part, something which shows discriminatory treatment and the intention to reserve the market for Brazilian firms," said Ordooz.
Roggio presented an official complaint to the Argentine Foreign Ministry to take up its case with the so-called protocol of conflict resolution under a Mercosur agreement.

The company said so far it has been treated in the same discriminatory way in privatization tenders in the Brazilian states of Rio de Janeiro and Paran. It has launched bids elsewhere in Brazil recently, but so far does not know what treatment it will get.

According to an internal Roggio memo given to Reuters, in Rio de Janeiro its subsidiary Caminos Australes was disqualified before the bidding started because the firm could not fulfill formalities that would be impossible under Argentine law.

In addition, Rio de Janeiro state claimed Caminos Australes did not have the required financial muscle to take part in the bidding. Despite this, Roggio says its subsidiary's bid was more "beneficial" than those of its rivals.

Still, according to Roggio, a Rio de Janeiro ruling states that it is necessary "to have as many bidders as possible to facilitate the public authorities' objectives of obtaining the most convenient services that are in its interests."
In the state of Paran, Roggio's subsidiary was given the same treatment. "These instances show discriminatory acts against Argentine firms," said the Roggio memo.
In Argentina, Roggio has concessions to operate tolls on 2,200 kilometres of the road network and a further 300 kilometres of motorways. It has annual revenues of $500 million.
